pr.title: Let Bit connect and set up repositories, with your tap
pr.body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"jasondwhyte"} -->
_Requested by **Jason** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01YGtEMFvZnSp5cxW5MGErkd?thread=cmsg_01YGtEMFvZnSp5cxW5MGErkd4yrx42V2CNrsAy6nSKB54b)_

Before: Bit could talk about your repositories and change Orbit's general settings, but connecting a repository or changing its setup meant going to Repositories yourself. Bit was also told never to touch a repository's setup command or network access.

After: you can ask Bit something like "set up acme/api". Its answer can offer a button:
- **Connect owner/name** appears for a repository GitHub lists that isn't connected yet. Tapping it downloads Orbit's own copy into its data folder with the GitHub CLI, then connects it with safe defaults: automatic reviews off, no setup command, no network, Codex as reviewer, and the copy kept up to date. Any change Bit listed is added on top.
- **Set up owner/name** appears for a connected repository. It can change the setup command, check command, network access, dev container, reviewer, round limit, approval wait, keep-copy-updated, or automatic reviews.

The button shows the exact change, including the full command, and nothing happens until you tap it. Trusted accounts stay off limits. Jason decided on 2026-10-11 to allow this, replacing the earlier rule that kept Bit away from repository setup.

How:
- **New `setup.rs`:**
  - `RepositoryPatch` holds the nine settings an answer may change. `patch()` accepts only values Repositories could save: one-line commands of at most 500 characters, booleans, a reviewer, and the offered limits.
  - A command is refused if it looks like a credential, uses curl, wget, sudo, ssh, scp, nc, base64 or eval, pipes into a shell, runs `git push`, or opens `/dev/tcp`. Bit is told the same; this check backs it up.
  - `clone_facts` reads the telltale files at the top of a copy: lock files, toolchain files and the dev container. From `package.json` it takes script names and the package manager, plain short names only, and it reads `package.json` only when it's a real file, not a link.
- **Question summary:**
  - Before the summary is built, `Engine::look_up` reads each connected copy (5-second limit) and lists your 100 most recently pushed GitHub repositories (10-second limit).
  - The summary shows each repository's setup and copy, plus up to 30 repositories that aren't connected.
  - An answer may only offer to connect a repository from that list.
- **Tapping a button:**
  - A button offered by an answer is checked again when it's tapped (`Repository::check`, split out of `Settings::validate`).
  - A connected repository is changed through `commit_settings`. Otherwise, while holding a new `cloning` lock, Orbit runs `gh repo clone` into `downloads/<owner>/<name>` and moves the finished copy to `clones/<owner>/<name>`. That way a download that was cut short is thrown away and never connected.
  - The repository is then connected with `save_repository`, which checks the copy's origin, and a sync starts.
  - The download runs in its own task, so closing the phone browser doesn't cancel it.
- **App:**
  - The button shows "Connect owner/name" or "Set up owner/name", the change in words (`describeRepositoryPatch`), and what connecting does.
  - The demo has a third sample button.

Checks:
- `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --no-default-features --all-targets -D warnings` pass.
- `cargo test --no-default-features`: 414 passed, 3 ignored dev-container tests.
- `prettier --check`, `eslint`, `tsc` and `vite build` pass.
- `vitest run`: 182 passed.

**F1 · P2 · Preserve the setup-versus-connect intent when a button becomes stale**

[Engine proposal dispatch, lines 371–378](https://github.com/analogproblems/orbit/blob/82c6ee9533eeb0a34dabaad079c6eb36446edb2e/src-tauri/src/engine/ask.rs#L371-L378) discards `Proposal.connect` when calling `set_up_repository`. **Breaks when:** Bit offers a **Set up owner/name** settings change for an existing repository, the person disconnects it in Repositories or another window, and later taps that old button. Orbit reconnects it (downloading a copy if necessary), enables keep-copy-updated by default, and can restore automatic reviews if that was in the patch. The old button only displays a settings change: the download/connect disclosure in `src/Buddy.tsx:204–211` is gated by `proposal.connect`, which is false here. The ordinary `save_repository(original=Some(...))` path already rejects a repository disconnected in the meantime.

**Needed fix:** carry the proposal's intended connect/setup mode through execution and revalidate it against current state. A setup-only proposal for a disconnected repository must fail and require a fresh connect proposal, rather than silently widening its action. Add a regression that offers setup, disconnects, then taps, asserting no clone, no repository insertion and no completed flag. Also cover state changes while awaiting the cloning lock/save.

- `a_repository_connected_during_the_download_gets_the_change_instead`: another window connects the repository while the download is still running. The result is one repository, at the other window's path, with the patch applied, and the button done.

**Other changes**
- The user guide and the architecture doc note both behaviours.

- Rust: `cargo fmt --check` and clippy with `-D warnings` pass; `cargo test` passes 416.

commit.message:
Let Bit connect and set up repositories, with your tap

Bit's answers can offer a Set up repository button. For a repository
GitHub lists that isn't connected, tapping it downloads Orbit's own copy
into its data folder with the GitHub CLI and connects it with safe
defaults (automatic reviews off, no setup command, no network) plus the
listed change. For a connected repository it changes the setup command,
check command, network access, dev container, reviewer, round and
approval limits, keeping the copy up to date, or automatic reviews.

To suggest a setup command, Bit's summary now includes each repository's
setup and the telltale files in its copy, such as lock files and a dev
container, plus up to 30 unconnected repositories. Commands from answers
must be one short line with nothing that looks like a credential, and
never fetch, pipe into a shell, raise privileges, reach other machines,
push or hide what they run. A download carries on if the window that
tapped goes away.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01EDJU2uY2NCz6Ch7CDHNcNA

Keep a settings button from reconnecting a repository

A Set up button that only changes settings now fails if its repository
was disconnected before the tap, instead of downloading and connecting
it again. A Connect button connects under the state lock, so a
repository connected from another window during the download gets the
change instead of a second entry.
